oidc_jwt.description: JWT profile grant assertions are documented as signed JWT authorization grants with freshness checks on exp/iat, but no jti replay tracking requirement is documented.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx and endpoints.mdx JWT Profile Grant sections
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT assertion may be accepted by a stateless verifier; do not flag replay_same_token without a documented one-time-use guarantee.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint is for authorized users and requires the access token of the user, not the client.
oidc_jwt.note: Failures when calling userinfo with client/service-account tokens are expected and should not be treated as identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than revocation or expiry.

oidc_jwt.description: Token endpoint responses may contain scopes that differ from the provided scope parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization-binding checks must compare granted scope/claims in the response, not assume echo semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope that is a subset of the original authorization; omitting scope reuses the original scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection of broadened scope on refresh is expected and should not be treated as a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Audience expansion beyond the documented subset is expected to fail by design.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims depending on the granted scopes; missing profile/email/custom claims without corresponding scopes is expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid flagging absent claims as authorization narrowing bugs when the scope was never granted.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may reject requested scopes that exceed the scope granted by the resource owner with invalid_scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Scope-expansion rejection is compliant behavior, not a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored and the default response mode for the response_type is used.
oidc_jwt.note: A fallback response mode is by design and should not be flagged as inconsistent flow handling.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT profile grant authenticates service accounts or applications and returns tokens for that machine principal rather than an interactive end-user session.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile; endpoints.mdx JWT profile response
oidc_jwt.note: Do not compare machine-token identities to human-user expectations from browser OIDC flows.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, exp in the future for control tokens, and iat not older than 1 hour. A valid control assertion should use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a control login, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from malformed JWT-profile setup.

For I1 trust-anchor and signature tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL identifies the signing key via the JWT header kid and validates the signature against the downloaded key/public key set. The attack JWT MUST keep a plausible kid value when testing wrong-key acceptance; otherwise failure may be caused by key lookup rather than signature verification.

For JWT profile grant assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, ZITADEL requires iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. This is a hard freshness rule from documentation, not an optional recommendation. Use {{now_epoch}} or {{now_epoch_minus_N}} with N<3600 for valid controls.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send exactly the same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL documentation states the token request redirect_uri must match exactly the authorization request redirect_uri; mismatches produce invalid_grant by design.

For I3 state-swap and code-injection tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD always include state, and the oracle must judge the callback/token outcome rather than identity comparison alone. ZITADEL returns the unmodified state to the redirect_uri; omitting state removes the session-binding signal needed for coherent OIDC flow testing.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send plain or alternate methods. A failed exchange without S256 is a setup error, not evidence about PKCE enforcement.

For I3 pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client hardening checks, assert non-200/error outcomes on exchange_code_for_token when code_verifier is omitted after a PKCE authorization request. Do NOT compare identities across users for these checks; they are flow-rejection tests.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If audience is outside that set, rejection is by design and not an I5 vulnerability. Build control subject tokens whose aud already contains the target audience before testing acceptance behavior.

For token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented token type matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only as subject_token when actor_token is also provided; refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Failures outside this matrix are by design.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, remember that token endpoint responses may return scopes that differ from the requested scope. Compare the returned scope and resulting claims, not just the requested scope string. Also, refresh_token grant scopes must be a subset of the original authorization scope when provided.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo returns information only for user access tokens, not client-only tokens. ZITADEL documentation explicitly says to send the access_token of the user, not the client. Using a client_credentials or service-account-only token against /oidc/v1/userinfo can fail by design and must not be treated as identity loss.

For introspect_token, active=true additionally depends on the requesting client being part of the token audience. A false/limited introspection result can be caused by audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than token invalidity. Use a client that is in the token aud for control introspection.

For revocation and introspection tests, ZITADEL documentation allows client authentication by either client_secret_basic/body credentials or private_key_jwt. If using private_key_jwt, include client_assertion and client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer; otherwise invalid_client may reflect missing client auth, not token state.

ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials. Do NOT emit login_with_password for oidc_jwt sequences; use authorization code/PKCE, JWT bearer grant, client credentials, or token exchange instead.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx: Resource Owner Password Credentials = no

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss equal to sub, exp in the intended test window, and iat not older than 1 hour. Otherwise token rejection may be caused by malformed assertion requirements rather than freshness enforcement. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 JWT bearer signature tests, the assertion header MUST include kid matching the downloaded key ID. Missing or wrong kid can cause rejection before signature-trust logic is exercised, confounding resign_attacker_key and trust-anchor tests.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 JWT bearer issuer/audience tests, ZITADEL requires assertion aud to include the issuing domain and requires iss/sub to identify the requesting service account or application. When testing issuer confusion, keep all other required claims valid so failures are attributable to the mutated field under test.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 authorization-code flow coherence tests, redirect_uri at /oauth/v2/token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. A mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and is not evidence of a session-binding flaw.

For I3 state-swap and code-injection tests, start_oidc_auth MUST send a unique state and the oracle must validate callback state equality. ZITADEL returns the unmodified state on success and error; missing state validation in the client would create false positives attributable to the test harness, not the broker.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method must be S256; this is the only supported algorithm. Do not vary the method when testing other invariants, or failures may be due solely to unsupported PKCE configuration.

For I3 and I5 token-exchange tests, audience requested in token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Rejection outside that subset is by design and must not be flagged as an authorization-binding success/failure for the wrong reason.

For token_exchange wrong-audience and ignore-audience tests, choose subject_token_type values from the documented matrix only. refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token; jwt is allowed only with actor_token; user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Using unsupported token types causes by-design rejection unrelated to audience enforcement.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange and refresh, requested scope must be compared against the original authorization. ZITADEL documents that refresh_token scope must be a subset of the original scope, and token exchange may return scopes differing from the requested scope. The oracle must inspect returned scope and claims, not assume echo semantics.

verify_granted_identity uses /oidc/v1/userinfo and only works with a user access token, not a client-only token. JWT bearer grant for service accounts may not yield meaningful human userinfo claims; use introspect_token as the primary verification step for machine-token sequences.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx userinfo_endpoint says use access_token of the user, not the client

oidc_jwt.constraint: Introspection success is audience-bound to the requesting client: active=true is returned only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience tests, a false active result can be caused by introspecting with the wrong client rather than by token invalidity.

Do not treat replay of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes stateless JWT bearer grant validation and does not mention jti replay tracking; repeated use may be accepted by design unless additional client-side constraints are configured.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx JWT profile grant; claims.mdx jti presence in access token/introspection

oidc_jwt.constraint: The revocation and introspection endpoints require client authentication by an authorization method or headers. Tests using revoke_session or introspect_token MUST supply valid client credentials (client_secret_basic, body client_id/client_secret where documented, or private_key_jwt) for the same client context, otherwise 401/invalid_client is expected by design.

For OIDC authorization requests, invalid response_mode values are ignored by ZITADEL. Do not use response_mode mutation as evidence of flow incoherence; the platform may silently fall back to the default response mode for the response_type.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss equal to sub, and iat no older than 1 hour. Use a CONTROL assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside the attack assertion; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by malformed JWT-profile requirements rather than freshness enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT MUST carry a kid header identifying the downloaded key. ZITADEL uses kid to identify the verification key; missing or wrong kid can cause rejection unrelated to the intended attack variant.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor and resigning tests against login_with_jwt, aud MUST still include https://{issuer_domain} and iss/sub MUST still match the service-account or application identifier. Only mutate the signing key or trust anchor under test; otherwise failures are ambiguous.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and code-flow coherence tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant if it differs, which is by design and not evidence of a session-binding flaw.

For OIDC code flow tests, start_oidc_auth SHOULD include state, and the fuzzer MUST preserve and compare the returned state on callback. Omitting state removes the documented CSRF/session-correlation mechanism and can make state-swap style results uninterpretable.
For implicit-flow start_oidc_auth requests, nonce MUST be provided. Missing nonce causes protocol-level rejection or altered behavior unrelated to the security property under test.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, start_oidc_auth MUST use code_challenge with code_challenge_method=S256 and exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier. ZITADEL documents S256 as the only supported method. Any other method or missing verifier yields protocol failure, not a security finding.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and must not be reported as inconsistent authorization behavior.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on token_exchange MUST be interpreted against ZITADEL's documented rule that invalid_scope includes scopes exceeding those granted by the resource owner. A rejection for expanded scope is expected behavior, not a bug.

For token_exchange token-type tests, only documented token type combinations are valid: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only as subject_token when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Invalid combinations must be treated as setup errors, not security findings.

For verify_granted_identity, the bearer token MUST be a user access token, not a client-credentials token. ZITADEL documents /oidc/v1/userinfo for the access_token of the user only; using machine tokens will not produce meaningful identity verification results.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. Therefore, introspection-based audience tests MUST authenticate as a client that is in the token audience for control cases; otherwise active=false is by design and not evidence of revocation or freshness failure.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication is required by the endpoint documentation. The fuzzer MUST supply either client_secret authentication or private_key_jwt (client_assertion plus client_assertion_type). A 401 invalid_client without client auth is a setup failure, not a revocation/introspection security result.

For I5 scope-driven claim tests, claims returned by verify_granted_identity and introspect_token depend on granted scopes. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes explicitly (for example email, profile, urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata, role scopes, audience scopes) before asserting missing or extra claims. Otherwise claim absence is by design.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud. The fuzzer MUST account for this default broad audience construction before flagging extra audience values as escalation.

No documented exact-match constraint parameters such as bound_subject, bound_audiences, or bound_claims exist for ZITADEL's JWT profile grant in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST NOT invent wildcard or exact-match semantics for nonexistent broker-side JWT constraint parameters in this protocol profile.
